summary: Regenerates the signed schema-epoch executable digest after the migration configuration boundary changed an inventoried source file.
userImpact: Release candidates can verify and publish the database-only migration runtime without weakening the signed schema-epoch bridge.

instructions: Use the matching host package, backend image, and Helm chart so every copy contains the same regenerated schema-epoch manifest.

configuration: No configuration changes are required; migration and preflight jobs continue to use only their database-scoped configuration and credentials.

notes: The executable migration ceiling, accepted ledger digests, PostgreSQL policy profiles, and all five TypeORM adapter behaviors are unchanged.
Only the source-content digest of the existing 16-file owner-transition implementation inventory changes.

security: The regenerated digest binds the database-only configuration import and deferred application-only seeding dependency introduced by the migration configuration boundary.
The manifest update command deterministically updates the canonical package copy and byte-identical Helm chart copy together.
documentation: The schema-epoch architecture documentation records the deterministic manifest write and verification workflow.
knownLimitations: Changing any of the 16 inventoried executable sources requires running the manifest write workflow and reviewing the resulting digest before candidate publication.
rollback: Revert this change together with the migration configuration boundary; do not combine the previous manifest digest with the updated migration runtime bytes.
validation: Manifest generation tests prove deterministic output, canonical/chart byte identity, source-mutation sensitivity, and verification against the regenerated digest.

The focused database-portability gate now verifies schema-epoch manifest integrity, and deterministic path classification sends manifest and generator changes through database qualification before release staging.
Focused schema-epoch, release-receipt, package, migration-boundary, and five-adapter tests preserve the existing runtime contract.
